definition: An April 1862 battle in Tennessee with about 23,000 casualties in two days, shocking the nation with how bloody the war would be.
An 1863 Virginia battle that was Lee's greatest victory, but where his best general, Stonewall Jackson, was mortally wounded by his own men.
An 1863 battle in Georgia where a mixed-up Union order opened a gap in the line, giving the Confederacy one of its last major victories.
A key Southern city captured by Sherman in 1864; its fall boosted Northern morale and helped Lincoln win re-election.
A victory that costs the winner so much that it almost feels like a defeat. Named after King Pyrrhus, who won battles but lost so many soldiers he could not keep fighting.
Completely defeating the enemy by destroying its army and its ability to keep fighting, rather than just winning one battle.
Carl von Clausewitz, a famous Prussian military thinker who wrote about how chaos and chance shape real wars.
A military idea from the thinker Clausewitz: real war is full of small accidents, confusion, and mistakes that no plan can fully control.
The period after the Civil War (1865 to 1877) when the United States tried to rebuild the South and decide the rights of newly freed people.
Bringing two sides back together peacefully after a conflict, instead of punishing the losing side.
Having to do with winning a single battle: the moves and decisions made on the battlefield itself.
Having to do with winning the whole war: the big-picture plan, not just one battle.
How confident and hopeful a group of people feels. High morale makes soldiers fight harder; low morale makes them want to give up.
The sense that one side is winning and gaining strength, which can make it harder for the other side to recover.
An attack: when an army moves forward to strike the enemy, instead of defending.
The vice president who became president after Lincoln's assassination. He was far less willing to protect the rights of freed people.
Members of Congress after the war who pushed hardest for equal rights and protections for newly freed Black Americans.
A politician who ran for office promising to end the war by making a deal with the South, instead of fighting on to victory.
A 'what if' question that imagines how history might have gone differently if one thing had changed.
A system of harsh, legally enforced racial separation in South Africa that lasted until the early 1990s.
A group set up in South Africa after apartheid to uncover past wrongs and help the country heal instead of seeking revenge.
Describing a society in the period right after a war or major conflict has ended, when it must rebuild and decide how to treat former enemies.
In a military sense, a battle plan carried out so skillfully that experts study it as a model of how to win.
Germany in the years after World War II, when it rebuilt and confronted the wrongs of the Nazi era - often studied as an example of a society facing its past.
